back: Budgeted overhead ÷ budgeted activity (hours, cost or units).
Direct labour hours, machine hours, percentage of direct labour cost, percentage of prime cost, units produced.
Actual overhead is known only after the period; prices are needed now, and a budgeted rate avoids month-to-month swings in job cost.
OAR × actual activity of the job, batch or unit.
Machine hours for machine-intensive work, labour hours for labour-intensive work, units for one standard product.
A rate per department, multiplied by the job's time in each, is more accurate than one rate for the factory.
Budgeted overhead ÷ budgeted direct labour cost (or prime cost) × 100; applied to the job's labour cost (or prime cost).
The total overhead does not change, but the base changes the share each job carries and so its cost and price.
Direct materials + direct labour + direct expenses.
